messages:
maria: incident-bot just paged: sudden spike in auth-verifier token validation errors (401/429) across eu-west-1 and us-east-1, paging oncall

incident-bot: [ALERT] service=auth-verifier check=token-verify error_rate=18.7% window=5m

ajay: seeing the same on our dashboards — token-verify latency up, internal API calls returning ~12% 401s. support queue filling with console login failures.

sam: digging into logs: upstream `auth0-edge` returning 429s from two POPs. example: `upstream_response_time=230ms status=429 url=/oauth/verify` across multiple zones.

jonathan: oncall here. priority 1: reduce customer-visible failures. maria, confirm JWKS behaviour in auth-verifier (local cache, TTL, serve-stale?).

maria: auth-verifier uses a JWKS cache TTL=15m and does a blocking fetch on miss. no serve-stale configured today; misses cause immediate fetch to auth provider.

kevin: quick mitigation plan: extend JWKS TTL to 24h, enable serve-stale-on-fetch-failure, and add one safe retry on 429s with exponential backoff. will canary to eu-west-1.

ajay: agreed. add small client-side retry: on 429 do one retry after 150ms then 300ms if needed, cap total for token-verification to 3s. should reduce churn and perceived failures.

jonathan: runbook I'm executing: 1) deploy JWKS_TTL=86400 to canary 2) set JWKS_SERVE_STALE=true 3) add 1 retry for 429s 4) watch metrics (2xx/401/429) and lower alert thresholds during rollout.

sam: initiating canary now. command: ```kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-verifier JWKS_TTL=86400 JWKS_SERVE_STALE=true && kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-verifier```

maria: do we want a temporary routing rule to direct verification calls away from affected POPs? that requires edge ops coordination; prefer local fixes first.

jonathan: agree. sam, notify when canary is up and post initial telemetry.

sam: canary live at 2256007995. preliminary: canary subset in eu-west-1 shows 63% reduction in 429s, median latency down ~30ms.

ajay: pushing retry logic to canary now. small code change in verifier, low blast radius.

kevin: retry change deployed at 2256008050 to canary. telemetry shows ~70% of 429s recovered on retry. effective error-rate in canary dropped to baseline.

maria: support reporting fewer tickets after canary. CS flagged three enterprise customers who hit timeouts earlier in the window (2256007600-2256007900). added them to impacted list for AM follow-up.

jonathan: if metrics remain stable we'll promote to full prod in 10m. also prepare a status page update: degraded auth verification due to third-party provider rate limiting; mitigations deployed.

statusbot: @channel incident status: investigating -> mitigating

ajay: drafted status page message: "We are experiencing increased authentication failures for a subset of customers in EU/US due to rate limiting at our external identity provider. We have deployed temporary mitigations (extended JWKS cache and retries) which have reduced errors for most customers. We continue to monitor and are working with the provider."

maria: opened ticket with Auth0 (ticket #245678) and escalated to their edge ops. they acknowledge protective throttling triggered in two POPs.

sam: running token-sweep to find any sessions with invalidated tokens during the incident window; will publish guidance for clients to retry auth calls if they saw failures.

jonathan: stakeholder impact summary for post-incident notes: - scope: approx 5-8% of interactive logins in eu-west-1 & us-east-1 were affected between 2256007600 and 2256007900 - severity: P2 (console access degraded, some API auth failures) - customer impact: 3 enterprise customers reported timeouts; dozens of users across various orgs experienced transient failures - mitigation: JWKS TTL increased, serve-stale enabled, 1 retry on 429 deployed, monitoring ongoing

kevin: postmortem action items: 1) request detailed rate-limit/mitigation logs from Auth0 (per-POP, per-endpoint) 2) add circuit-breaker in auth-verifier to avoid retry storms 3) add feature to seed JWKS on deploy to prevent cold fetch storms 4) add synthetic checks that detect provider throttling (early warning)

maria: I'll add a runbook entry in ops/incidents/auth-dependencies with exact steps and safe defaults to flip JWKS TTL and enable serve-stale.

ajay: question: fallback to alternate provider (Auth0 -> Okta) is a major lift and requires contract+mapping work; recommend as a long-term project only for high-availability customers.

jonathan: agreed; not in scope for this incident. I'll stay on to hand off to AM shift at 2256008400.

sam: full rollout completed at 2256008200. metrics stable for 10+ minutes, 429s returned to baseline.

maria: Auth0 updated: protective policy triggered by an edge anomaly in two POPs, fix rolled at 2256008250. they confirm no key integrity issues and are reviewing thresholds.

jonathan: closing notes: incident lead jonathan, sam handles deploys/metrics, kevin writes postmortem, ajay handles customer comms. next steps: draft postmortem, update runbooks, follow up with Auth0 on concrete rate-limit guidance.

kevin: starting postmortem draft and will share doc for comments. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: status changed -> resolved (monitoring)

maria: handing off to AM shift with notes and tasks. thanks everyone.

statusbot: status.redwood.ai updated: "Degraded auth verification — mitigated. Retry + cache changes deployed; provider rolled a fix. Monitoring."
